Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing a formal consumer complaint against Caine & Weiner Company , Inc. for direct non-compliance with the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g, and CFPB Regulation F ( 12 CFR 1006.34 ) governing debt validation requirements. For transparency, a prior complaint regarding this account was closed after Caine & Weiner represented through the portal that supporting verification documentation would be provided via mail. This current complaint stands as a separate, distinct escalation concerning the fact that the documentation subsequently mailed completely fails to satisfy federal verification standards. On XX/XX/year>, I submitted a formal written Debt Validation Request explicitly demanding three specific categories of records : ( 1 ) A complete transaction history and itemized accounting explaining the calculation of the alleged {$550.00} balance ; ( 2 ) Documentation supporting the underlying consumer obligation with the original creditor ; and ( 3 ) Documentation establishing Caine & Weiners legal authority to collect and furnish information concerning this specific account. Under CFPB Regulation F ( 12 CFR 1006.34 ), a debt collector must provide a consumer with clear, itemized data if requested. Caine & Weiners mailed response completely failed to meet these mandates. They provided only a generic cover letter and a single-page XXXX final bill summary. Crucially, Caine & Weiners own correspondence explicitly admits that the balance differences are the result of adjustments made to the account by the creditor. Despite making this representation, the company completely failed to include any transaction history, payment ledger, or underlying records identifying those adjustments or explaining how they affected the balance now being asserted. A summary final billing statement that merely lists a total amount completely fails to satisfy verification obligations under 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) when a consumer has explicitly disputed the underlying calculations and accounting entries. Furthermore, demanding a balance that relies on un-itemized, hidden 'adjustments ' constitutes a direct violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 2 ) ( A ) for misrepresenting the true legal character, nature, and amount of an alleged consumer debt. To further demonstrate their total lack of data integrity, the XXXX billing statement relies on an incorrect historical address ( XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, PA ) that completely contradicts my current verified address. By continuously furnishing and verifying this unvalidated, mathematically inconsistent data to the consumer reporting agencies without possessing the underlying ledger records to substantiate it, Caine & Weiner is also operating in direct violation of Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) data accuracy standards under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ). Because Caine & Weiner has completely failed to provide the mandatory itemized accounting, underlying obligation data, and collection authority records required to substantiate this debt, yet continues to actively collect on this unvalidated account, I request that the CFPB require Caine & Weiner to immediately cease all collection activity and permanently delete this non-compliant, unverified tradeline from all nationwide consumer reporting agencies.
